text: KH/RT initial growth and independent linear references Compare actual small-amplitude nonlinear2D runs with separately derived continuous Fourier–Galerkin linear IVPs. Separate finite-time growth, spatial, temporal and amplitude effects. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-instability-growth-2026-11-23-r2 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. KH initial growth in a smooth periodic shear layer Evolve the actual nonlinear2D vorticity PDE and compare finite-time growth and spatial errors with an independent continuous Fourier–Galerkin linear IVP. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Periodic[0,2pi]², layer width.25, nu=kappa=.005, epsilon1e-5 and32²/64²/128² grids. Explicit forcing maintains the base. U=tanh(sin y/delta),T1. Editorial clarification Small-amplitude fixed educational cases. The independent reference changes spatial representation but linearizes the PDE; it is not a second nonlinear engine. No sharp-interface infinite-domain dispersion, original compressible McNally inputs, late roll-up or RT turbulence claim. Figures explicitly normalize computed perturbations by epsilon. Adopted numerical method Advance point-sampled perturbations using centered shared-face conservative fluxes and Heun; invert the five-point Poisson symbol by FFT. Centered derivatives define divergence-free velocity.
